learning: Pending the race. If slalom steering_oscillation falls below 0.16 without a progress loss, damping is a usable lever. If the oval and s-bend metrics still match iteration 9 to four decimals, the controller damping and geometry are both exhausted for the line-loss problem.
notes: Iteration 10 package: the iteration-9 geometry frozen as requested, with kd raised from 0.05 to 0.2 as the only controller change. Compare against iteration 9 (36.6227) to isolate damping on the slalom oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 9 is the best-scoring platform (36.6227). It keeps the Builder's ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at y = 0.07 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 × 0.18 m, and narrows wheel_track to 0.10 m. Its gain over iteration 8 came only from the slalom: max_error 0.0681 m, steering_oscillation 0.1611 and slalom score 46.12. The oval and s-bend are unchanged across every geometry family tested (max_error about 0.061 m, one line-loss event per trial, no finishes). The 0.06 m off-track floor binds, and body_width cannot lift it. Mass 0.5 kg (iteration 7) lowered slalom oscillation but also lowered slalom progress and the score, so mass stays at 0.8 kg. The only lever that has moved the score is controller gain: kp 3.0 raised the slalom from 14.39 to 45.18. The Builder's feedback asks for a damping test (kd near 0.2) to address the slalom oscillation of 0.161, which is just above the 0.16 threshold. I therefore keep kp 3.0, ki 0, and the iteration-9 weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), which match x/0.02 steering gain. I set kd to 0.2 as the only controller change, so any change against iteration 9 comes from damping. last_direction line-loss handling is kept, since no evidence yet shows where line loss starts. Expected, not measured: slalom steering_oscillation should fall below 0.16 with little progress loss, and the oval and s-bend are not expected to change much, because the line-loss mechanism has not responded to any controller change except kp.
